summary.one_liner: HashiCorp Vault is a tool for securely accessing and controlling access to secrets such as API keys, passwords, and certificates, with audit logging.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Vault as a secrets management tool that stores arbitrary key/value pairs and encrypts them before writing to persistent storage (disk, Consul, and others). It can generate dynamic secrets on demand for systems such as AWS or SQL databases and revoke them when their lease expires. It supports lease renewal through built-in APIs, revocation of single secrets or trees of secrets, and encryption/decryption of data without storing it. The README is mostly a project overview with developer notes: building from source with make targets, running unit tests (which require Docker), running acceptance tests against real backends, and Docker-based cluster test helpers in Go. It also links the documentation, tutorials, and the vault-examples repo.
use_cases: centralize storage of API keys and passwords
generate short-lived database or AWS credentials on demand
rotate and revoke secrets after an intrusion
encrypt data from applications without writing custom crypto
build and test Vault from source
how_to_run: Install Go and set GOPATH/GOBIN (per README)
make dev  (builds the Vault binary into bin/)
make testacc TEST=./builtin/logical/consul  (acceptance tests; use at your own risk, they touch real resources)
notable: Dynamic secrets that are auto-revoked after their lease ends
Encryption-as-a-service: encrypt and decrypt data without storing it
Revocation of a whole tree of secrets, e.g. everything read by one user
Docker-based test cluster helpers in the sdk for multi-node and replication tests
caveats: Acceptance tests create and modify real resources and may incur costs
Importing the main repo as a Go dependency is not a supported use
Enterprise features are referenced but not documented in this README
